teams.heading: L'Équipe and RugbyPass blame Fiji's indiscipline and execution for Italy defeat
teams.body: Friday's 23-21 defeat to Italy in the 11th-place final at Twickenham drew pointed verdicts abroad. L'Équipe argued Italy owed their survival solely to Fijian indiscipline, punished by Tommaso Allan's 68th-minute penalty, and to a granite defence inside their own five metres that held to the final whistle. RugbyPass found Fiji's late push thrilling but judged imprecise execution decisive. TNT Sports called the fightback from 17-0 down to lead 21-20 remarkable, with Fiji outscoring Italy three tries to two.

lead.why: The result has already run, so the foreign press verdict on why Fiji lost is the strongest genuinely new angle.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones mocks England's 'mess' critics after record win over All Blacks
teams.body: Japan's head coach used the I Love Rugby podcast to take a sarcastic swipe at journalist Owen Slot, whose pre-November piece claimed the environment around Borthwick's squad was worse than ever and that players complained in July about his man-management. "You go back two weeks ago and England were a mess," Jones said, then credited a powerful carrying and clean-out display against New Zealand, said Itoje looks to have his spark back and rated Fin Smith's short kicking game probably the best in the world for a 10.

lead.why: Fresh, England-centred and the most talked-about item not already run: Eddie Jones's barb at England's critics after the record win over the All Blacks.

teams.heading: Tani Vili and Gaël Dréan among 14 released by France staff
teams.body: Toulon can pick Dréan and Mathis Ferté at Clermont on Sunday night. The pair are among 14 players released by the France staff before the Nations Championship final against South Africa at Twickenham. Stade Français regain Vili, Léo Barré and Louis Carbonel, while Nicolas Depoortère is free to face Montpellier with Bordeaux-Bègles. Five reservists stay with the squad: Moses Alo Emile, Esteban Capilla, Guillaume Cramont, Paul Graou and Thomas Laclayat. That leaves Bayonne without Capilla and Cramont against Castres.

teams.heading: James McNabney marks second Ireland cap with two tries against Australia
teams.body: The Ulster back-row came off the bench in Friday's 38-14 win at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, and crashed over twice in the closing minutes to put the fifth-place final beyond the Wallabies. Planet Rugby named him among its winners, arguing Andy Farrell has to keep giving him Test minutes on the strength of his size and gainline carrying. His brace completed a five-try night that sealed four wins from four in November, with Robbie Henshaw, Nick Timoney and Rob Baloucoune also crossing.

lead.why: McNabney's two tries off the bench on his second cap are the standout fresh Ireland storyline not yet run, distinct from the Prendergast, Stockdale and captain's-run editions.

teams.heading: Tommaso Allan's boot carries Italy past Fiji 23-21 to end losing run
teams.body: Friday's 11th-place final at Twickenham avenged last week's 21-16 defeat in Udine. Converted tries from Federico Mori and replacement Giacomo Nicotera had Italy 17-0 up early, but Fiji outscored them three tries to two and edged ahead 21-20 through Kitione Salawa. A scrum penalty on the edge of Fiji's 22 let Allan land his fifth kick from five with 13 minutes left, and defence on their own line did the rest. It is Italy's first win since beating England in March's Six Nations.

lead.why: The result is the day's fresh Italy event, it ended a seven-match losing run, and both outlets covered it.

teams.heading: Townsend's Scotland face Argentina at Twickenham, first British meeting away from Murrayfield
teams.body: All 11 previous meetings between the sides on British soil were played at Murrayfield: 10 full Tests between 1990 and 2025, plus an uncapped Scotland match in 1973. The seventh-place final is also the third and last meeting of the World Cup cycle, and Scotland won July's encounter in Córdoba 47-38. Americas Rugby News reports that Townsend is treating the match as a transition towards Australia 2027, where Scotland are second seeds in Pool D with Ireland, Portugal and Uruguay.

teams.heading: Sam Costelow wins Wales No. 10 battle, starting against Japan at Twickenham
teams.body: The Scarlets fly-half pairs with Reuben Morgan-Williams in Saturday's ninth-place play-off at Twickenham, with Dan Edwards absent from the named replacements. It caps a turbulent Test career: Warren Gatland dropped Costelow after one match following the 2023 World Cup, Ben Thomas and Gareth Anscombe have each moved ahead of him since, and the online criticism at times turned vitriolic. He has spent the past 18 months contesting the jersey with Edwards, and the pair embraced after the 35-28 win over New Zealand.

lead.why: It carries the confirmed Wales XV for Japan, and Costelow's place at No. 10 is the fresh selection story the reader has not yet seen.

teams.heading: Contepomi drops Facundo Isa and moves Scelzo to No. 8 for Scotland
teams.body: Joaquín Moro takes the openside shirt for Sunday's seventh-place final against Scotland at Twickenham, a reshuffle that leaves Facundo Isa out of the 23. Up front, Rodrigo Martínez replaces the injured Boris Wenger alongside captain Julián Montoya and Francisco Moreno. In the backs, Isgró takes over from Bautista Delguy on the wing, and 22-year-old Faustino Sánchez Valarolo starts at inside centre ahead of Justo Piccardo, who drops to the bench.

teams.heading: Kalani Thomas marks first Test start with try in defeat to Ireland
teams.body: The scrum-half's second-half score came from a support line off Josh Canham. He also made 48 metres after nearly having his first clearance charged down. The try only briefly stalled Ireland in Friday's fifth-place play-off at Allianz Stadium. Lock Jeremy Williams had burrowed over for a deserved 23rd-minute lead before Ireland replied with 24 unanswered points either side of half-time. Carter Gordon converted both Australian tries, while debutant James Ramm endured a difficult night on the left wing.

lead.why: A fresh Australia angle on Friday's result. Thomas's first Test try on his first start is new, unlike the already-run Jorgensen HIA.

teams.heading: Dylan Riley leaves Japan squad for son's birth before Wales final
teams.body: Riley's departure, confirmed this week, takes another name off Eddie Jones' list for today's ninth-place final against Wales at Twickenham. Ryosuke Iwaihara and Seina Kimura were both ruled out after the 67-5 defeat by Scotland. Several players from the side beaten 28-21 in Cardiff on 7 November are also no longer in the mix, so a thinned group carries a four-match losing run into the decider.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson defends under-fire Tana Umaga over All Blacks' missed tackles
teams.body: Defence coach Umaga has drawn criticism after New Zealand shipped five tries apiece to Wales and England. The former wing told Sport Nation that last weekend's 32 missed tackles were not Umaga's fault: "The players missed the tackles." He also cited selection churn through the outside backs caused by injury, and insisted the staff are not at the point of a mid-cycle change. In his view, only a really poor showing against England in Saturday's Nations Championship finale could shift that conversation.

lead.why: Freshest New Zealand-specific story: a former All Black backs the under-fire defence coach before the England finale.

teams.heading: Pieter-Steph du Toit's niggle hands Paul de Villiers the No. 8 jersey
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has had to rejig his loose trio for Sunday's Nations Championship final against France at Twickenham after Du Toit was forced to withdraw earlier this week. Cameron Hanekom switches to blindside flank alongside captain Siya Kolisi, with De Villiers now at the base of the scrum. The Boks need a win to avoid a third successive Test defeat for the first time since 2021 and to finish the year ranked No. 1. Franco Mostert comes onto the bench in De Villiers' place.

lead.why: A late injury withdrawal that reshapes the Springbok loose trio for the final is the freshest South Africa team news.
